title: How to Find Your Average Monthly Salary Australia: Hourly to Annual with Casual Loading and Super
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week. Includes casual loading, super, tax, and the average monthly salary Australia from ABS data.
salarySummary: For a casual employee on the national minimum wage ($33.05/hr including 25% loading), the annual gross is about $65,318.60 before super and tax, based on a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. If you are casual, add 25% loading first (e.g., $30 × 1.25 = $37.50/hr) before the calculation. Superannuation is paid on top of this amount at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base.

faqs.q: What is the average monthly salary in Australia?
faqs.a: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). To get a monthly figure, multiply by 52 and divide by 12: approximately $9,029 per month. This is a benchmark for full-time employees. For all employees including part-time, average weekly total earnings are $1,579.20, giving a monthly average of about $6,843. The national minimum wage ($26.44/hr) yields a monthly gross of about $4,354 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (sick leave, annual leave). For example, if the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, a casual employee must be paid at least $33.05 per hour. This loading is included in your hourly rate before calculating annual salary. Superannuation is then calculated on your ordinary earnings (including the loading) at 12%. Always check your award or agreement, as some awards have higher casual loadings.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Understanding your annual salary from an hourly rate is straightforward: multiply your hourly pay by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This gives your gross annual earnings before tax and superannuation. For most full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. We use this assumption throughout unless your contract specifies otherwise.

### The 38-Hour Week Assumption

The national system defines a full-time week as 38 ordinary hours. When you see a weekly rate like $1,004.90 (the national minimum wage from 1 July 2026), it is based on 38 hours at $26.44 per hour. If you work more or fewer hours, adjust accordingly. For part-time or casual roles, your agreed hours per week may differ, but the calculation method remains the same.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the national minimum wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees are covered by an industry or occupation award, which often provides higher minimum rates. Always check the relevant pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman to find your correct classification and rate.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the national minimum wage, this means $33.05 per hour. **Important:** When converting your hourly rate to annual pay, if you are casual, apply the loading first. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading into a calculator expecting a separate loading checkbox—our timesheet lets you toggle the 25% loading on your base rate.

Superannuation (super) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (the super guarantee rate for 2026–27). It is not deducted from your salary; your employer contributes it separately. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year, so super stops accruing on earnings above that threshold. For example, on a $65,318 casual annual salary, super adds about $7,838 per year.

### Understanding the Average Monthly Salary in Australia

While pay periods in Australia are typically weekly or fortnightly, you may want to compare your earnings to the **average monthly salary Australia**. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 (May 2026). Multiplying by 52 and dividing by 12 gives approximately $9,029 per month. This is a useful benchmark for full-time roles. For all employees (including part-time), the average weekly total earnings are $1,579.20, or about $6,843 per month.

To find your own monthly equivalent, calculate your annual salary as described, then divide by 12. For a casual on the national minimum wage ($33.05/hr, 38 hours/week), annual gross is $65,318.60, so monthly is about $5,443. Remember, this is before tax and super.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Most residents also pay a 2% Medicare levy. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a detailed estimate. Note that HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included here.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

If you are paid fortnightly, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For the national minimum wage, weekly is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80. For a casual, weekly is $1,255.90 (33.05 × 38), fortnightly $2,511.80. These figures are gross; your employer will deduct tax and any other authorised amounts.

### Practical Example

Let’s say you are a casual employee on an award rate of $30 per hour (base). You work 38 hours per week. First, add 25% casual loading: $30 × 1.25 = $37.50 per hour. Annual gross = $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100. Super at 12% = $8,892 (paid on top). Monthly gross = $74,100 ÷ 12 = $6,175. After tax (using 2026–27 rates and Medicare), your take-home pay would be roughly $55,000 per year, or $4,583 per month. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to run your own numbers.

### Important Disclaimer

This article provides estimates. Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more details, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page or browse [pay guides](/blog) for your award.
